reasons: A Vendor-side IP indemnity does exist: Section 13 (p0090) has Garman warranting it owns/controls all rights necessary and expressly agreeing to 'indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless' for all Losses (including settlement amounts and reasonable legal fees) from breach of that warranty, plus the standard infringement remedies (procure the right, procure an equivalent element, replace/modify) — this meets the fallback's material terms.

The clause is one-sided in our favour: there is no reciprocal Customer indemnity and no Customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs, and Section 15 expressly disapplies the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion to Section 13, so the indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. Flagging this as a deviation would be over-flagging.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact: the indemnity is expressed through breach of the ownership/rights warranty rather than the words 'indemnify ... against claims that the Work infringes', with 'infringement' appearing in the remedies sentence. Substance satisfies the rule.

Correctly no redline and no counterparty comment for a compliant finding; the shortfalls versus preferred (no express duty to defend/control, no refund remedy, no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct limbs, tight ten-day notice) are properly noted in the rationale as sub-elements rather than raised as deviations.
